answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; shuffle each entire tier before dealing.

answers.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game. Both setups give 2 Agents on the Leader and the Swordmaster beside the board, 12 troops total with 3 in the garrison and 9 in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: Score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents; 3 troops in garrison, 9 in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents, and after Revealing you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns, so cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed in the Reveal step, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up, move all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns; Reveal Turn: resolve Reveal boxes of just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: A Plot Intrigue played before placing the Agent may grant resources that are then available for the entry cost. Resources from the played Agent card or destination, which occur only after placement, cannot pay that same cost. One card sends one Agent using one of its icons; it cannot send multiple Agents. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns entry-cost timing; Agent Turn: choose only one Agent icon; no Agent icons means Reveal only.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, you may deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from the garrison, for 5 total. At a non-Combat space you do not deploy troops. Recruited troops come from your supply into your garrison; if supply is empty you cannot recruit more.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: newly recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison, at a Combat space; cube recruits from supply to garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets an Agent go to any space connected to one of your Spy-occupied observation posts without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player's Agent on the destination; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after Agent placement and before any space or card effects to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both; you may use two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence. Choose Gather Intelligence immediately after placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon; Infiltrate; Gather Intelligence timing; cannot recall same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2 = 4, plus 1 sandworm × 3 = 3, plus 4 swords = 11. If your last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You cannot play Combat Intrigue without at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; need at least one unit. Intrigue cards: Combat only with a unit deployed.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again after an opponent plays; the window closes when all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Phase 3 Combat: players may play or pass; not required to pass just because passed earlier; all pass consecutively closes. Cleanup destinations stated.

answers.answer: With two tied for first in four-player play, each receives the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody takes the Conflict card. The same first-place tie in a three-player game gives each tied player the second reward, with no other reward; nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat and Conflict ties by player count; 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards; two worms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For an optional reward of 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay a second 3 spice for a second VP (6 spice total for 2 VP).
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more doubles; location control and battle icons excluded; optional cost may be paid again.

answers.answer: After you win and take the Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. A matching icon pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP; matching is mandatory. At Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons; winner's card procedure orders taking card first, then checking mandatory match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you later fall below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP. Tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance; you must rise above their Influence. The Alliance VP follows its holder and transfers away if lost.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: Faction Influence; retained track bonus versus temporary Alliance VP; tie does not steal.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after effects. You may pool Persuasion from sources for one purchase and split one source among purchases; unused Persuasion is lost. Buy Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card at its top-right cost. After a Row purchase, replace it from the Imperium Deck and you may buy the replacement if able. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal turn purchases, timing, pooling/splitting, replacement, destination, unused Persuasion lost.

answers.answer: At Makers, each Maker space without an Agent gains 1 bank spice in its bonus spot, accumulating until visited; a visitor gains all bonus spice. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. A worm can never go in a garrison; Shield Wall prevents summoning to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin until removed.
answers.evidence: Phase 4 Makers; Sandworms and Sandworm Reward Doubling; board-space table: Deep Desert, Hagga Basin.

answers.answer: Endgame triggers at the end of a round if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare VP. Tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5 Recall; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup shuffles the 20 standard contracts and exposes 2 face up, leaving 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and 4 additional Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left out; they are not part of the 20 standard tokens.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module setup changes; contrasting-back contracts are separate Rise of Ix compatibility set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM and contracts available, the icon takes one of the two face-up contracts and replaces it with a face-up token from the bank; without CHOAM, or once all contracts have been taken, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the stated spice total that turn; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts; Completing contracts; Human contract icon shared rule.

answers.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract for a space you already visited that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must hold it when you send the Agent. On completion announce it, gain its rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: already visited space must wait; completion procedure.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; eligible Objective cards are randomly dealt to the humans, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective goes first. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: setup, turn order, Agent turns.

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: attempt an empty post of the specified type, ignore placement if none exists, then immediately reveal another card and continue the Agent turn. Ignore normal space costs and effects; apply only the Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs and effects.

answers.answer: In 3–4-player setup, omit Objectives with a player-count marking that does not match, shuffle the eligible cards, and give one face up to each player; the marked card determines First Player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so not without it.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5; Shaddam is used only with CHOAM.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, and water are not limited: substitute conveniently if the bank runs out; the supply of sandworms is likewise not meant to be limited. Troops are limited by the personal supply: if it is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Payments of Solari, spice, or water go back to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: resources and sandworms not meant to be limited; payments return to bank. Recruiting & Deploying Units.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card, resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws 5 cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, or in two-player play return Rival Agents to its supply and pass First Player to the other human, then start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases; Phase 1; Phase 5 Recall.

answers.answer: Yes, after paying entry cost and meeting requirements, space effects, Agent-box effects, and the Faction advance may be carried out in any order. No: the destination's Influence is gained after placement, so it cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs before resolving effects; effects may be in any order; Faction advance on Faction space.

answers.answer: No. An arrow cost/effect may be used only once per turn, except sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward. Most effects are mandatory; “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are optional. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play the Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ & Rulings: Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy on an unoccupied observation post; if all your Spies are deployed, you may first recall one for no effect. If the placement effect requires a particular Agent-icon type connected to the post, the post must meet that requirement or you cannot place there.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy icon placement and specified Agent icon restrictions.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. Recalling a Spy for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence does not replace the need to play an appropriate card for an Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; the same placement permits at most one Gather Intelligence, though another Spy may be used for Infiltrate.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ Spies.

answers.answer: A location's controller gains its visit bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. A Conflict winner places/replaces the Control marker. When the Conflict for a controlled location is revealed, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Agent-turn defensive troop bonus; board-space table.

answers.answer: In a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner retains their reward and Conflict card, and there are no further rewards. Players tied for third get nothing. Three tied for first each get the second reward; nobody wins or takes the card and no other reward is given.
answers.evidence: Combat ties; Conflict ties by player count.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their printed rewards; third gets nothing. This also applies in two-player play with a Rival, since that is a three-competitor game.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second receive rewards; third gets nothing unless tie for second.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigue may be played during your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigue only during Combat and only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigue at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck; after resolving one, place it face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified. Secrets' steal icon takes one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has 4 or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play; trashed ordinary cards go to the box, while Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card directs you to trash itself. The VP from acquiring The Spice Must Flow remains even if it is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once at the moment you acquire the card. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards; Acquire box; FAQ Victory.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. A Fremen Bond effect works if one or more other Fremen cards are in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to discard.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent sent this turn; it can be used again on a later Agent turn in that round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” permits zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect that gains two Influence must put both with one chosen Faction; it cannot split them. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated minimum with its named Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: gain two free choice cannot choose different Factions; Alliance and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which of the previously tied opponents receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Victory Points / Alliance loss FAQ.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the normal five-card draw. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until then, is used, and then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If you receive one as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: If all resource tiebreakers also tie, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

answers.answer: No. All contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement; you cannot delay them. Contract effects are another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, provided you held each contract when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: No, Shaddam does not start with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts; he may choose one instead of a generally available one when acquiring a contract, and only Shaddam may take them. His Signet Ring deployment restriction applies immediately on the Agent turn when he plays Signet Ring and lasts for that turn only.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup; Reserved Sardaukar contracts; Shaddam's Signet benefits; FAQ Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost Training-track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ & Rulings.

answers.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, and reaching 2 with the same Faction may trigger again after losing Influence and later moving up to 2; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, is not a Faction, and always draws one card; its contract icon gives 2 Solari without CHOAM, takes/replaces a contract when CHOAM has contracts available, and gives 2 Solari when all are taken. It gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, gives 1 Emperor Influence total (automatically as an Emperor space), and resolves that same contract-icon rule; it does not grant a second Emperor advance beyond the one listed.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: contract spaces and Faction status table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits 1 troop and draws 1 card, while controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw 1 card. Research Station: City, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit 2 troops and draw 2 cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon 2 sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon 1 sandworm. Both choices also collect all bonus spice there. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Deep Desert and Hagga Basin; Sandworms; FAQ Spies.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit 1 troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, is not a Combat space, and costs 5 Solari each visit. On your first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit 3 troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone has one and 6 after anyone obtains one; it is once per player per game. Take the third Agent from beside the board to your Leader, available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, costs 3 Solari, and is not a Combat space. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, recall one of your other Agents, and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege; Recall Agent icon.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, and is not a Combat space. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit 2 troops either way, and gain 1 water if you paid 2. Spice Refinery uses City access, is Combat; choose to pay 0 or 1 spice, gaining 2 Solari or 4 Solari if you pay 1. Its controller also gains 1 Solari on any visit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, Combat yes, costs 5 spice; gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit 5 troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen, Combat yes, costs 1 water; gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1 troop, optionally trash a card. Sardaukar: Emperor, Combat no, costs 4 spice; gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue, recruit 4 troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, costs nothing, is not Combat; draw an Intrigue, and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, is not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild, costs nothing, is not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it can be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes on the bottom Influence spaces, 3 troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, 2 Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, 3 Spies, 1 water, and score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and place it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall just like a human's score, and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Rival can win.

answers.answer: As soon as its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends exactly that many resources and takes its third Agent, available in the current round. It counts each unit/card as one and must spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water, using as much of each type as needed. It keeps all leftovers and cannot choose a different mix to save higher-priority resources.
answers.evidence: Swordmaster resource total; spending priority is mandatory.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot combine a mixed total of seven resources for a VP.
answers.evidence: After Swordmaster: whenever Rival has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost Faction in its priority list; numbered Hagal Influence icons refer to positions in that priority list. It gets the ordinary 1 VP at 2 Influence and an Alliance token's 1 VP if it holds it. At 4 Influence it does not receive the track bonus resource.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: Faction Influence; After Swordmaster; Rival Combat: Influence choice; Hagal numbered Influence.

answers.answer: No. Use only the destination matching current conditions; if it is occupied, reveal a new Hagal card and do not use the other destination. Guild Influence selects Accept Contract or Shipping; Conflict tier selects Deliver Supplies or Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination card conditions and occupied destination.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to 2 available garrison troops even if the card recruited none; newly recruited troops also deploy there. At a noncombat space, recruited troops go in its garrison. If it lacks 2+ Influence for a conditional bonus, that bonus is omitted but does not prevent placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and conditional bonuses.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. The Rival never recalls Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival visits a Combat space that turn, those newly recruited troops deploy there too. If a Place Spy card finds no legal empty post, ignore placement and immediately reveal another Hagal card because the card has not sent an Agent.
answers.evidence: Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards do not place an Agent.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival collects all bonus spice. With its own Hooks and a Conflict that allows worms, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of taking base spice. If it summons none, it takes base spice (2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert); without Hooks or when Shield Wall protects that Conflict, it cannot summon. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. Hooks remain on its garrison.
answers.evidence: Maker spaces: Rival; Hooks and Wall icons; board-space table.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords as strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival does not get this bonus.
answers.evidence: Combat: Rival.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival receives normal rewards, doubles them with one or more sandworms, wins Conflict cards and battle-icon VP normally, gains control bonuses on visits and defensive troops when its controlled Conflict is revealed. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Combat: Rival.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; update it as needed while resolving the turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn; Strength.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal the card. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader abilities; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It does not by itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate effects you may choose without a card when recalling a connected Spy.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon versus Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction is a card of your choice from your hand, but cannot be an Intrigue unless it specifically allows it.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: A sandworm-doubled reward that grants 1 Influence of your choice gives two Influence; this is a doubled reward, and the example allows the same or two different Factions. By contrast, a single effect that says gain two Influence with a free choice requires both with one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice rule.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the Rival card. Do not substitute its Scheme; no human Signet Ring card or Reveal turn is involved.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme are separate abilities.

answers.answer: A Hagal Maker Hooks icon takes a Hooks token if the Rival lacks one and does nothing if it already has one. Shield Wall removal works only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks, ignore it, and if the Wall is already gone there is no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives one selected at random from their own Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice. If the visitor controls it, the controller also gains 1 spice, so that same player receives that additional 1 spice.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin; controlled locations.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards left from earlier rounds. Each player draws five cards after the Conflict is revealed and any defensive troop bonus is resolved.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. Place the four Alliance tokens on the marked areas of those tracks; normal setup assigns no Alliance to a player. The Shield Wall token begins on the marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6; Maker Hooks assigned to bank.

answers.answer: The player holding First Player starts, and turns proceed clockwise. In normal 3–4-player play, Player Turns end when all players have taken a Reveal turn. During Combat Intrigue, start with First Player and proceed clockwise; each eligible player with at least one unit may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass, and can act again after another player plays, until all involved pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 Player Turns; Phase 3 Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: The three steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, Clean Up. Reveal all remaining hand cards; resolve only those cards' Reveal boxes in any order (not necessarily card order), use Persuasion during this step, and then Clean Up all cards in front of you to discard.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three steps.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and place it face down by the Leader. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM cards, shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, deal 5 Imperium cards face up to the Row, and place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Each human Combat marker starts at 0; 3 Spies, Councilor, and Control markers start in that player's supply; each Influence cube starts on the bottom of its track.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; Initial card states.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, spend Persuasion to acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, at the cost shown at the card's top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases are made on your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when legal. Shield Wall destruction is optional; once removed, the Wall is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: ordinary placement/recall optional; Shield Wall.

answers.answer: The played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination's access icon, or a Spy Agent icon with your Spy at a connected observation post. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a City-only card access Shipping. If the card itself has the Spy Agent icon, your connected Spy permits the Agent to go to that connected space without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: matching icon; Spy Agent icon access rule.

answers.answer: Yes. You may play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent, and resources it grants then can pay the entry cost. Resources gained only after placement from the Agent card or destination cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot Intrigue and entry cost timing.

answers.answer: No. Even after both humans Reveal, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has Agents in supply; begin Combat only when both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 Player Turns: two-player play.

answers.answer: When that location's Conflict is revealed at Round Start, its controller may deploy one troop directly from supply to the Conflict; it is optional and requires no Agent visit. After Conflict rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 defensive troop bonus; Phase 3 cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space (subject to Spy rules); resolve its Agent box, not Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card in play or discard as the played card, nor simply move an Agent already on the board; the turn's Agent is sent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Reveal Turn Clean Up; setup places Agents on Leader.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately on playing Signet Ring to send the Agent, so he cannot deploy units on that turn by resolving the board space first. The restriction cannot be postponed by changing effect order.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Shaddam's restriction takes effect immediately; FAQ Shaddam.

answers.answer: First, second, and third place receive their printed rewards; fourth place receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card (then checks for a battle-icon match).
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with four players ordinary first, second, and third receive rewards; winner takes card.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select them at random.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: choose a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed; you cannot choose a card directly from your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival. Retain the 2P Reshuffle card; it is not removed.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup.

answers.answer: All 4 Maker Hooks tokens start in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A token later acquired moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise changes strength, adjust the participant's Combat marker when the card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. Combat rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track, not a fixed Reveal-turn value.
answers.evidence: Phase 3 Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Take gained Solari, spice, and water from the bank. You do not take them from another player's supply; payments of these resources return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: gain from bank; payments return to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip 2 face up onto the marked offer spaces and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. The offers and bank order are randomized, not chosen or preset.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module setup changes: shuffle remaining standard contracts face down, flip two offers, rest face down in bank.

answers.answer: Before shuffling, set aside both Sardaukar contracts; only Shaddam may acquire them, and they do not begin in his possession. Shuffle the other 18, expose 2 face up, and leave 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts set aside separately.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
